subject: MAP performance playbook and acceptance gates for Helix Research
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@helixresearch.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: MAP performance playbook and acceptance gates for Helix Research

Oliver,

Attached is our proposed performance section for the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) tailored to Helix Research's evaluation needs. High-level goals are below; the attached workbook (helix_map_perf_spec.xlsx) contains the detailed workload slices, test matrix and acceptance gates.

Scope highlights:
- Workload types: interactive chat (avg 256 tokens), batch summarize (avg 2048 tokens), long-context ingest (up to 8k tokens)
- Targets: TTFT p95 < 350ms (interactive), throughput 350 req/s sustained for mid-size payloads, concurrency testing up to 128 parallel sessions
- Success criteria: pass all SLOs on our hosted infra or proposed Dedicated config for the 30-day pilot

Asks from Helix:
1) Confirm the three workload slices and token distributions.
2) Any additional payloads or regulatory constraints we should include (data residency, logging level).
3) Target decision date so we can align run windows (you mentioned late October).

We propose an initial benchmark run the week of Oct 18th; Marissa/Aditya will own execution. Please review and let us know.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: helix_map_perf_spec.xlsx

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@helixresearch.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixresearch.ai>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@helixresearch.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T14:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: MAP performance playbook and acceptance gates for Helix Research

Kimberly,

Thanks for the detailed draft — this looks like a solid starting point. A few notes from our side:

- Workloads: please add a "mixed-burst" slice to capture real-world session behavior (bursts of short interactive followed by occasional long context).
- TTFT requirement: interactive p95 < 300ms would be ideal for our UX team; if that is not realistic we need clear trade-offs.
- p99 performance: we require p99 data for all slices (for compliance with our SLA commitments).
- Data residency: final logs and audit traces must remain in-us; we will provide the target region.

Procurement is pushing for an executed agreement by Oct 29th. To keep that cadence we need benchmark evidence (runs and raw metrics) no later than Oct 21st so internal legal can review the performance claims. Can you confirm you can deliver the raw CSVs and a short runbook link by then?

Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Platform Engineering | Helix Research
procurement@helixresearch.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-13T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP performance playbook and acceptance gates for Helix Research — test plan

Kim / Aditya —

We can run the initial benchmark windows the week of Oct 18 as proposed. Proposed test matrix (short summary):

1) Workload slices
  - Interactive: 80% single-turn chat, token dist median 256 (max 1024)
  - Batch summarize: avg 2048 tokens, batched requests (batch sizes 8/16)
  - Long-context: ingest and retrieval at 4k and 8k token windows
  - Mixed-burst: synthesized sessions with 70% short turns, 30% long tails (to mimic Helix telemetry)

2) Configurations
  - Model variants: open-20b-fp16, open-20b-int8, redwood-rlhf-20b-quant
  - Hardware: H100 (dedicated) and A100 (hosted) profiles
  - Batching: dynamic continuous batching, static batch sizes 1/8/16
  - Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 32, 64, 128 parallel workers

3) Metrics collected
  - TTFT (time to first token) p50/p90/p95/p99
  - Latency per token, end-to-end tail latencies
  - Throughput (req/s), tokens/sec, GPU util, KV cache hit rate
  - Error rates, retries, OOM events

Acceptance gates (proposal)
- Interactive: TTFT p95 <= 350ms (goal 300ms), p99 <= 900ms
- Batch: sustained throughput >= 300 req/s for 2048 token avg with p95 latency <= 1s
- Long-context: successful runs at 8k without functional errors; p95 TTFT < 800ms
We'll publish a public runbook (runbook_redwood_bench.md) and share raw CSVs after the runs. I recommend an overnight run window to stabilize GPU cache/warm-up effects.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@helixresearch.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Results: Helix MAP benchmark run (summary + artifacts)

Oliver / Kimberly —

We completed the primary benchmark runs on 2026-10-19 (hosted A100) and 2026-10-20 (Dedicated H100 profile). Attached: benchmark_results_20261020.csv and a snapshot of the KPI dashboard (kpi_dashboard_screenshot.png). Full runbook link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-HelixMAP

Top-line summary (short):
- Interactive (256 token median)
  - Hosted A100: TTFT p95 = 330ms, p99 = 870ms; throughput peak 380 req/s at concurrency 64 with steady-state ~340 req/s
  - Dedicated H100: TTFT p95 = 280ms, p99 = 760ms; sustained throughput 420 req/s at concurrency 64
- Batch (2048 tokens)
  - Sustained throughput: 310 req/s (A100), 360 req/s (H100) with p95 latency 920ms (A100) and 740ms (H100)
- Long-context (8k tokens)
  - Functional success on H100 with p95 TTFT = 760ms; on A100 we saw intermittent OOM errors at concurrency >= 8 (captured in CSV)
- Mixed-burst
  - Observed higher p99 tails (~1.1s) driven by background cache churn during burst spikes; KV cache hit rate averaged 78% in those runs.

Acceptance gates vs proposed:
- Interactive: p95 targets met on Dedicated H100 (280ms) and close on Hosted (330ms). Customer goal of 300ms is met by Dedicated but not hosted.
- p99: tails exceed Helix's stricter desire (<300ms) — p99 remains an area to address.
- Batch & Long-context: H100 meets proposed gates; Hosted will require config changes (larger instance, tuned quantization) or Dedicated option.

Recommendations / mitigations
1) To lower p99 tails: enable prefix KV caching for hot sessions and increase warm-up windows; we saw p99 reductions of ~18% in targeted re-runs.
2) For hosted parity: offer a dedicated H100 pool for the pilot or white-glove tuning (quantization profile redwood-rlhf-20b-quant+KV).
3) Provide the raw CSV and dashboard to Helix procurement/legal for their review (attached).

Next steps requested:
- Oliver: confirm whether Dedicated is acceptable for the 30-day pilot and whether Oct 29th signature timeline still stands.
- Kimberly: if procurement needs an explicit p99 commitment, we should document a fallback SLA and a remediation plan.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: benchmark_results_20261020.csv, kpi_dashboard_screenshot.png

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@helixresearch.ai>, Procurement <procurement@helixresearch.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Results: Helix MAP benchmark run (summary + artifacts) — acceptance gates and close runway

Oliver / Team,

Appreciate the quick review. Based on the runs and the mitigations Aditya outlined, Redwood can support the following MAP commitments:

- Acceptance gates: we will sign the MAP with the Dedicated H100 configuration as the baseline for the 30-day pilot. Dedicated meets interactive p95 (280ms) and batch/long-context gates per the proposed thresholds.
- p99 commitment: we will include a remediation clause tied to KV caching and warm-up tuning; initial p99 targets documented as follows: interactive p99 <= 900ms during pilot, with an aim to reduce <700ms within 30 days of tuning.
- Delivery artifacts: raw CSVs, dashboard snapshot and runbook will be delivered (links shared) to Procurement/legal by Oct 23rd.
- Timeline: target contract signature by 2026-10-29; pilot start week of Nov 8 (provisioning and onboarding scheduled Nov 1-5).

Please confirm acceptance of the Dedicated baseline and the p99 remediation path. Once we have procurement sign-off, I will circulate the MAP with the performance section locked and the close plan attached.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198
